reason: The text introduces Job (אִיּוֹב - Iyov) by name as a man (אִישׁ) who lived in the land of Uz. He is portrayed with distinctly human characteristics: he has a wife, seven sons and three daughters, possesses livestock and servants, engages in family gatherings and feasting, and performs worship rituals. While the broader narrative context involves supernatural elements (God and Satan), Job himself is presented as a regular human being with normal family relationships, property, and responsibilities—not as a deity or supernatural entity.
